object.label: A UMI collision occurs when the same UMI labels reads from two or more distinct molecules.
Modular, efficient and constant-memory single-cell RNA-seq preprocessing
object.description: Single-cell RNA-seq preprocessing quantifies transcript or gene abundance in individual cells. Experiments can span 10^6 to 10^10 reads, while existing workflows can require extensive time and disk space or memory that grows with dataset size. kallisto-bustools achieves near-optimal speed, constant memory, scaling to arbitrarily large datasets, Cell Ranger-consistent downstream analyses, and fast RNA-velocity analysis.

relations.statement: This publication contains this grounded claim.

evidence.span: UMI collision estimates. A UMI associated with a read from a cell is said to have 'collided' if it appears in two or more reads originating from different molecules. To estimate UMI collision rates, two types of information were used. First, reads in the same cell that originate from different genes must have originated from different molecules, and therefore the sharing of a UMI between two such reads was used as an indicator of a collision. Second, for each gene, the number of distinct UMIs associated within it was measured from the data. Based on the assumption that UMIs were sampled uniformly at random from beads, these data were used to estimate the number of intra-gene collisions (see Supplementary Note). The assumption was verified by examining the distribution of UMI counts across cells; the empirical distribution was near uniform with the exception of a handful of UMIs (Supplementary Note Fig. 2).

evidence.span: Comparative analysis of the 10x Genomics E18 mouse dataset. Analysis of the Cell Ranger and kallisto bustools preprocessed datasets was performed in R. The DropletUtils package33,34 was used to remove empty droplets from the kallisto bustools gene count matrix. For Cell Ranger, the filtered matrix was used. After filtering, genes not detected in any remaining Cell Ranger or kallisto bustools barcode were removed. Seurat was used for basic analysis. First, data were normalized by dividing the UMI count of each gene in each cell by the total UMI counts of that cell, and the result was multiplied by 10,000. Then a pseudocount of 1 was added, and the natural log transform was applied. Subsequently, the normalized data were scaled so the distribution of the expression of each gene would have a mean of 0 and a standard deviation of 1. Subsequently, 3,000 genes with highly variable expression levels were selected with the vst method in Seurat. Then principal component analysis was performed on these genes in the scaled data with the R package irlba called by Seurat. The first 40 principal components were used for t-SNE, which was performed with the R package Rtsne called by Seurat. Clustering was performed with the Leiden algorithm29 on the kallisto bustools and Cell Ranger matrices. The clustering parameters were 20 nearest neighbors and resolution 1. Differential expression analysis was performed with the logistic regression method described in Ntranos et al.31 as implemented in Seurat and applied to the normalized (unscaled) data. Spearman and Pearson correlations were computed for the top 15 cluster marker genes. GSEA was performed on cluster marker genes with adjusted P <0.05 using the R package topGO35 with the GO36,37 annotations provided by Bioconductor 3.10. SingleR38 was used to annotate cell types based on correlation profiles with bulk RNA-seq from ref.39 . Then, the neuronal cell types were used for pseudotime analysis. Pseudotime analysis was performed with slingshot40 via the Docker container from dyno41 .

evidence.span: To demonstrate the flexibility of our approach we also processed 2,799 A549 lung carcinoma cells expressing nuclease-dead Cas9–Krüppel-associated box (dCas9–KRAB) assayed with the 10x Genomics CRISPR screen kit, and transduced with 90 sgRNAs targeting 45 different genes. Assessing the multimodal tradeoff
object.description: Multimodal assays can register chromatin accessibility and gene expression in the same cells, simplifying connections between the two measurements. Assessing tradeoffs across technologies requires uniform processing because distinct assay read structures complicate cross-platform comparisons. snATAK produces results concordant with Cell Ranger while running much faster, and its uniform processing identifies technology-choice tradeoffs in multimodal single-nucleus genomics.

relations.statement: This publication is cited in support of this claim.

evidence.span: After read cataloging and error correction, the final step in universal preprocessing is read counting. To quantify the number of features per cell in single-cell genomics assays, molecular counting approaches must be applied in a manner that balances accuracy, speed, and memory while being consistent between assays that do, and do not, have UMIs. We leverage the kallisto bustools counting approach as it performs UMI and read counting in a consistent way. This means that UMIs quantified in scRNAseq data are resolved in a manner that is consistent with reads quantification for scATAC-seq data (Sina Booeshaghi, Gao, and Pachter 2023).

object.label: Universal preprocessing of single-cell genomics data
object.description: Large single-cell atlases depend on comparing datasets generated by many assays, so preprocessing must be consistent before biological interpretation begins. Existing workflows are often assay-specific, while read structures, barcode correction, and UMI/read counting differ across RNA, ATAC, protein, tags, and spatial modalities. cellatlas uses machine-readable seqspec files to configure modular tools for uniform preprocessing across nine datasets, modalities, and single-cell technologies.

Deciphering the impact of genomic variation on function
object.description: Genomic variation can reveal mechanisms of human biology and genetic predisposition to disease. Understanding how variants alter genome function and phenotype remains challenging without a systematic catalogue of their effects. IGVF combines single-cell mapping, genomic perturbation, and predictive modeling across hundreds of cell types and states, integrating the resulting data, predictions, standards, and pipelines into an open resource.

object.label: The impact of genomic variation on function (IGVF) consortium
object.description: Human genomic variation influences molecular and cellular functions as well as disease-related phenotypes. Understanding how variation alters genome function remains challenging, and interpreting genomic variation requires a systematic catalog of genome function and molecular and cellular variant effects. The IGVF Consortium brings together more than 120 laboratories to integrate single-cell mapping, systematic perturbation, predictive modeling, and a preliminary variant-effect map spanning gene expression, protein activity, and molecular networks.

object.label: Isoform cell-type specificity in the mouse primary motor cortex
object.description: Isoform regulation is crucial for neuronal differentiation and is implicated in neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric disease. Most single-cell brain studies rely on gene-level measurements, which can mask cell-type isoform shifts. Linking SMART-seq isoform resolution with 10x Genomics-defined cell types and MERFISH spatial measurements revealed extensive cell-type-specific isoform diversity in mouse primary motor cortex and refined cell types beyond gene-level estimates.

object.label: Nicolas Bray
kallisto, bustools and kb-python for quantifying bulk, single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq
object.description: RNA-seq assays quantify RNA species from bulk tissue, single cells, or single nuclei. Preprocessing must map reads, handle assay-specific barcodes and UMIs, and support mature or nascent RNA quantification across assay types. kallisto, bustools, and kb-python provide free open-source workflows that produce gene-expression quantifications from raw reads for bulk, single-cell, and single-nucleus RNA-seq.

object.label: The impact of package selection and versioning on single-cell RNA-seq analysis
object.description: Standard single-cell RNA-seq workflows rely heavily on Seurat and Scanpy for filtering, dimensionality reduction, clustering, and differential expression. Although the packages are thought to implement similar steps, they produce substantially different outputs. Package differences are comparable to analyzing under 5% of reads or under 20% of cells, while version changes also produce substantial differences that are especially pronounced in differential expression.

relations.statement: Nicolas Bray is an author of The impact of package selection and versioning on single-cell RNA-seq analysis.

object.label: The impact of package selection and versioning on single-cell RNA-seq analysis
object.description: Most single-cell RNA-seq analyses use Seurat or Scanpy across a multistep workflow. Package implementations and versions can silently change results and downstream interpretation. Seurat and Scanpy differed across multiple workflow stages by amounts comparable to using 5% of reads or 20% of cells, while version changes particularly altered differential-expression results.

relations.statement: Nicolas Bray is an author of The impact of package selection and versioning on single-cell RNA-seq analysis.

object.label: Voyager: exploratory single-cell genomics data analysis with geospatial statistics
object.description: Spatial organization is central to tissue function, and exploratory spatial data analysis can reveal structure in single-cell genomics data. Decades of geospatial methods have not been fully adapted to standard spatial-omics workflows. Voyager provides local, bivariate, and multivariate spatial methods through a common interface, a geometry-aware data structure, reproducible tutorials, and consistent R and Python implementations, revealing signals such as biologically relevant negative spatial autocorrelation.

object.label: Determining gene specificity from multivariate single-cell RNA sequencing data
object.description: Multivariate single-cell experiments can assay gene specificity across sex, tissue, age, genotype, and cell state. Existing specificity measures largely overlook multivariate structure or fail to decompose coherently across hierarchical partitions. Ember supplies three entropy-based metrics and is the only method shown to satisfy four desired specificity properties, revealing context-dependent markers, housekeeping genes, strain-driven cell-type switching, tissue-dominated mouse variation, and cell-type-dominated human PBMC variation.

relations.statement: Barbara Wold is an author of Determining gene specificity from multivariate single-cell RNA sequencing data.

object.label: Long-read sequencing transcriptome quantification with lr-kallisto
object.description: Definitive full-length isoform quantification would extend RNA measurement beyond affordable gene-level short-read counts. Long-read data properties, isoform complexity, genetic variation, and much higher error rates create bioinformatic challenges. lr-kallisto makes pseudoalignment feasible for long reads while retaining efficiency and accurately quantifying biological and simulated data across error rates.

relations.statement: Barbara J. Wold is an author of Long-read sequencing transcriptome quantification with lr-kallisto.

object.label: Long-read sequencing transcriptome quantification with lr-kallisto
object.description: Long-read sequencing platforms can support full-length isoform quantification, but isoform complexity, genetic variation, and long-read error profiles create computational challenges. Efficient methods are needed to accurately associate long reads with transcripts of origin across current long-read data types. lr-kallisto accurately and efficiently quantifies long-read RNA-seq libraries, supports bulk, single-cell, and single-nucleus data, benefits from exome capture, and uses less memory than compared long-read tools.

relations.statement: Barbara J. Wold is an author of Long-read sequencing transcriptome quantification with lr-kallisto.

object.label: Systematic cell-type resolved transcriptomes of 8 tissues in 8 lab and wild-derived mouse strains capture global and local expression variation
object.description: Cell-type-resolved expression maps can connect genomic variation to complex traits and disease predisposition. An 8-cube of 5.2 million nuclei across eight tissues and 106 cell types and states showed transcriptome variation tracking genetic divergence, with tissue-dependent and cell-type-concentrated strain effects that highlighted immune and metabolic differences.

object.label: Massively scaled-up testing for SARS-CoV-2 RNA via next-generation sequencing of pooled and barcoded nasal and saliva samples
object.description: Asymptomatic and presymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infectivity makes molecular screening important for pandemic control. RT-qPCR capacity, result delays, RNA extraction, and approximately US$100 test costs limited widespread regular testing. SwabSeq uses pooled next-generation sequencing with barcoded nasal or saliva samples and synthetic RNA standards to run extraction-free testing with qPCR-comparable performance, under-24-hour turnaround, and more than 80,000 returned results.

object.label: Modular, efficient and constant-memory single-cell RNA-seq preprocessing
object.description: Single-cell RNA-seq preprocessing quantifies transcript or gene abundance in individual cells. Experiments can span 10^6 to 10^10 reads, while existing workflows can require extensive time and disk space or memory that grows with dataset size. kallisto-bustools achieves near-optimal speed, constant memory, scaling to arbitrarily large datasets, Cell Ranger-consistent downstream analyses, and fast RNA-velocity analysis.

relations.statement: Massively scaled-up testing for SARS-CoV-2 RNA via next-generation sequencing of pooled and barcoded nasal and saliva samples cites Modular, efficient and constant-memory single-cell RNA-seq preprocessing.

object.label: Reliable and accurate diagnostics from highly multiplexed sequencing assays
object.description: Scalable, inexpensive, and secure SARS-CoV-2 testing is crucial for pandemic control, and highly multiplexed sequencing assays are promising alternatives to RT-qPCR tests. Their clinical use requires reliable analysis, interpretation, and computational workflows that handle sample indices, biological targets, gene counts, and infection-status classification. A kallisto-bustools workflow processes recently proposed sequencing-based diagnostic tests quickly and with low memory, validates SwabSeq analysis against an orthogonal workflow, and extends to assays with different targets and sample-index structures.
